title: Schisandrin B alleviates sulfolane-induced liver injury via the APOA1/ROS/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Xing, Yuechen; Zhang, Bo; Jin, Shuo; Guo, Youtong; Chen, Yueru; Chen, Lili; Wang, Yue
one_liner_zh: 该文研究五味子乙素通过APOA1/ROS/NF-κB通路缓解环丁砜肝损伤，属毒理学与信号通路研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Sulfolane is a widely used industrial solvent and emerging groundwater contaminant. Sulfolane has hepatotoxicity, but the molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Schisandrin B (Sch B), a bioactive lignan isolated from Schisandra chinensis, has been shown to exert hepatoprotective effects. To elucidate the mechanisms underlying sulfolane-induced liver injury and to determine whether Sch B protects against this toxicity by modulating the APOA1/ROS/NF-kappaB signaling axis. Male C57BL/6 J mice were administered sulfolane (0, 10, 30 or 300 mg/kg) by oral gavage for 28 d, with or without Sch B (8 mg/kg). Liver injury was assessed using histopathology, serum biochemistry, hepatic lipid deposition, ROS levels, and inflammatory marker expression. Bioinformatic analyses integrating "sulfur compound" and "liver injury" datasets were used to identify candidate pathways. The protective effects of Sch B were investigated through APOA1 gene knockdown, APOA1 overexpression, treatment with the antioxidant NAC, and molecular docking experiments of Sch B with APOA1. Sulfolane caused dose-dependent steatosis, oxidative stress and inflammation in mouse liver and AML12 cells. sulfolane suppressed APOA1, increased ROS and activated NF-kappaB and downstream cytokines. Sch B restored APOA1 expression, reduced ROS accumulation and NF-kappaB-dependent cytokine production, and markedly improved biochemical and histological indices of liver injury in vivo and in vitro. Sulfolane-induced hepatotoxicity is mediated by suppression of APOA1 and subsequent activation of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway in a ROS-dependent manner. Schisandrin B protects the liver against this injury by modulating the APOA1/ROS/NF-kappaB axis.
abstract_zh: 环丁砜是一种广泛使用的工业溶剂，也是新兴的地下水污染物。环丁砜具有肝毒性，但其分子机制仍知之甚少。五味子乙素（Sch B），一种从五味子中分离出的生物活性木脂素，已被证明具有保肝作用。为阐明环丁砜诱导肝损伤的机制，并确定Sch B是否通过调节APOA1/ROS/NF-kappaB信号轴来保护免受该毒性影响。雄性C57BL/6 J小鼠通过口服灌胃给予环丁砜（0、10、30或300 mg/kg）28天，联合或不联合Sch B（8 mg/kg）。通过组织病理学、血清生化、肝脏脂质沉积、ROS水平和炎症标志物表达评估肝损伤。整合“硫化合物”和“肝损伤”数据集的生物信息学分析用于识别候选通路。通过APOA1基因敲低、APOA1过表达、抗氧化剂NAC处理以及Sch B与APOA1的分子对接实验，研究了Sch B的保护作用。环丁砜在小鼠肝脏和AML12细胞中引起剂量依赖性的脂肪变性、氧化应激和炎症。环丁砜抑制APOA1，增加ROS，并激活NF-kappaB及下游细胞因子。Sch B恢复APOA1表达，减少ROS积累和NF-kappaB依赖性细胞因子产生，并在体内和体外显著改善肝损伤的生化和组织学指标。环丁砜诱导的肝毒性通过抑制APOA1及随后以ROS依赖性方式激活NF-kappaB信号通路介导。五味子乙素通过调节APOA1/ROS/NF-kappaB轴保护肝脏免受该损伤。
